messages.subject: dplyr method wanted
parts:
Hi D-RUG folks.

I have a data manipulation task that a I have a way of doing, but I would like to be able to do it with dplyr, if possible, and I am currently stumped.

I have a data frame of all the nights of sleep (or naps) recorded by five people, including the date and the sleep duration in hours.

require(lubridate)

require(dplyr)

nights.all <- 

  data.frame(person.id = c(1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 3, 3, 3, 4, 5, 5, 5, 5),

             record.date = ymd("2009-09-17", "2009-09-18", "2009-09-20", "2010-02-23",

                                "2010-03-01", "2009-07-03", "2009-07-03", "2009-07-04",

                                "2009-07-05", "2009-07-07", "2011-11-30", "2010-04-16",

                                "2010-04-17", "2010-04-18", "2010-04-21"),

             sleep = c(8.2, 7.1, NA, 5.4, 6.7, 0.6, 7.2, 6.8, 7.5, 6.8, NA, 6.1, 6.2, NA, 7.3))

I extracted the rows that meet criteria for an analysis I want to do into a different data frame, called nights.

nights <- nights.all[c(1, 2, 4, 7, 8, 9, 11, 12, 14, 15), ]

I would like to add a column to the nights data frame containing, for each row, the total amount of sleep obtained on the prior date, if available.  Here is how I am currently doing this:

nights.list <- split(nights, nights$person.id)

nights.all.list <- split(nights.all, nights.all$person.id)

prior.sleep <- 

  mapply(function(x, y) 

           {sapply(x$record.date, 

                   function(z) 

                     {ifelse(length(which(!is.na(y$sleep[

                               which(y$record.date == z - days(1))]))) > 0, 

                             sum(y$sleep[which(y$record.date == z - days(1))],

                                 na.rm=T),

                             NA)})},

         nights.list, nights.all.list)

nights$prior.sleep <- unlist(prior.sleep)

Can anyone suggest a way to do this using dplyr instead?

Thanks.


Bonnie

messages.author: b35e99045f6c74c2
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: dplyr method wanted
parts:
Are there duplicated observations per person per day? e.g. two separate entries for the same person on the same day? This doesn't seem to the case in your test data, and makes life easier. Here's a quick test:

> any(duplicated(paste(nights$person.id, nights$record.date, sep="-")))
[1] FALSE

Then, we could use lag(), one of dplyr's window functions: 

> nights %>% group_by(person.id) %>% arrange(record.date) %>% mutate(prior.sleep=lag(sleep, order_by=record.date))
Source: local data frame [10 x 4]
Groups: person.id

   person.id record.date sleep prior.sleep
1          3  2009-07-03   7.2          NA
2          3  2009-07-04   6.8         7.2
3          3  2009-07-05   7.5         6.8
4          1  2009-09-17   8.2          NA
5          1  2009-09-18   7.1         8.2
6          2  2010-02-23   5.4          NA
7          5  2010-04-16   6.1          NA
8          5  2010-04-18    NA         6.1
9          5  2010-04-21   7.3          NA
10         4  2011-11-30    NA          NA

Is that what you're looking for?

If you do have duplicates that would require summing sleep across duplicated person-days, I would merge these beforehand using dplyr. You could probably do this without merging (using RcppRoll or something), but I would keep it simple.

HTH,
Vince

messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: dplyr method wanted
parts:
Thanks, Vince.  It is good to know about the lag() function.  

In this case, there are sometimes repeated sleep recordings by the same person on the same date (such as the nap in row 6 of nights.all), so I would like to sum those.  There are also many dates when sleep was not recorded, so I will probably need to retrieve the sleep data by date, rather than using lag() (unless there is some way of getting lag to understand that I don't want anything in cases where the previous date does not exist for that person).  

Also, I should have been more clear that I would like to get the data on prior sleep from the nights.all data frame, because sleep obtained on the day before an observation would still be relevant even if the day before did not, itself, meet criteria for inclusion in the analysis.  So, part of what I am trying to figure out is a way to get dplyr to retrieve data from a different data frame while staying within the grouping by person.id in the data frame it was given.  I tried the following as a quick test of that idea, but got an error, so I guess dplyr doesn't work the way I am trying to use it.

> group_by(nights, person.id) %>%
+   summarize(n.all=length(which(nights.all$person.id==person.id)))
Error in which(c(1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 3, 3, 3, 4, 5, 5, 5, 5) == person.id) : 
  object 'person.id' not found

Bonnie
